title: The Evening Brief: Manchester City guilty; Arizona State under review; Giants cut Beckham
dek: An independent commission found Manchester City guilty of 114 of 115 Premier League financial charges spanning nearly a decade. Arizona State placed its hockey coach on leave following a player's collapse and calls for independent investigation. The Giants released Odell Beckham Jr. after three games and zero catches.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Wednesday brought three major organizational reckkonings: Manchester City's verdict on systematic financial misconduct, Arizona State's internal crisis forcing external pressure, and the Giants' failed experiment with a franchise icon returning at 34.
bottom_line: Manchester City's guilty verdict marks a milestone in Premier League enforcement, but the severity of sanctions remains undetermined until an appeal hearing concludes by late January. Arizona State faces October 9 as a checkpoint: if the Board of Regents declines to commission independent investigation, pressure will likely intensify from lawmakers and the NCAA. Beckham's release at 34 reflects a broader reality for aging receivers; Reed's season-ending neck injury reshapes Green Bay's receiving room. Brooks' arraignment on October 28 will test whether a 0.0 breathalyzer reading holds in court.
body: Three separate institutions faced accountability Wednesday, each at a different stage of resolution.

The Manchester City finding is the most complete. An independent commission concluded that the club created sham sponsorship agreements and received disguised owner funding totaling more than £900 million from 2009 through 2018, violations the commission said artificially increased revenues and reduced costs across those nine seasons. Specific evidence included modified sponsor agreements generated within days of May 2013 to plug a £9.9 million shortfall before a financial year ended, and the Fordham Arrangement involving inflated player image-rights payments. The club denies all accusations and says it possesses "irrefutable evidence" of innocence. City has until Friday, October 4, to file its appeal to a three-person board; a decision is due by the end of January 2027. Premier League CEO Richard Masters called it the most significant case in league history. The commission has authority to impose points deductions, transfer embargoes, and expulsion, though the reporting does not specify what sanctions it may recommend.

Arizona State's crisis remains open and contested. Coach Greg Powers was placed on paid administrative leave Wednesday, three days before the season opener, following the August 20 collapse of sophomore Matthew Mayich during an outdoor workout. Seven rostered players sent a 26-page letter to university president Michael Crow disputing the school's preliminary report and calling for external investigation, citing fear of retaliation from coaches. Mayich's parents agreed that the coaching staff should be placed on leave, and family attorney Rob Carey said the action is insufficient because assistant coach Mike Corbett remains in the locker room. Two Arizona Republican lawmakers requested the Board of Regents retain an independent investigator with an October 9 deadline for response; U.S. Senators Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego also called for independent review. The National Collegiate Hockey Conference stated the concerns "deserve to be heard and thoroughly reviewed." No external investigation has been launched. Arizona State Police is conducting an internal inquiry; the Maricopa County Attorney said Tuesday she will not take over. Powers issued a statement supporting the leave and pledging cooperation. The reporting does not state what the independent investigation, if commissioned, would examine or when it would conclude.

In professional sports, two roster decisions reflected the arc of aging receivers. The Giants released wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. on Wednesday after he played 20 offensive snaps across three games and recorded zero catches. Head coach John Harbaugh said the team could not find a way to make the fit work and framed the decision as a roster need rather than a reflection on Beckham. The Giants signed Braxton Berrios and Charlie Jones to address the spot. Beckham, drafted by New York in 2014 and holder of 5,476 receiving yards and 44 receiving touchdowns in Giants colors, had hoped to rewrite his final chapter; he will not return to the practice squad and is seeking immediate employment elsewhere at 34. Hours before Beckham's release, the Packers announced that wide receiver Jayden Reed will miss the entire 2026 season due to a neck injury sustained in Week 2 against the Jets on September 20. Reed, the team's leading receiver for two years and signee of a $50.25 million contract extension in April, was placed on a backboard and carted to a local hospital for overnight evaluation. The reporting states he had movement in his extremities after the injury but does not specify the prognosis for recovery after surgery.

Two other moves addressed depth. The Padres added right-hander Joe Musgrove to their Wild Card roster against Chicago; Musgrove has not pitched in the majors since October 2, 2024, following Tommy John surgery for a torn UCL and a back injury that delayed his return. Should he pitch, it will be his first game action in nearly two years. The Suns' Dillon Brooks was formally charged Wednesday with one count of DUI, a Class 1 misdemeanor, stemming from a March 6 traffic stop in Scottsdale. Bodycam footage showed Brooks blew 0.0 on a breathalyzer, though officer accounts reported signs of impairment and a vehicle that smelled like a dispensary. Brooks is due for arraignment on October 28, one week after the Suns open their regular season. The reporting does not explain the grounds for the charge given the zero breathalyzer result.

In the front office, Colorado promoted Andrew Cogliano from special assistant to assistant general manager. Cogliano, a 2022 Stanley Cup champion with the Avalanche, will work alongside GM Joe Sakic across all areas of hockey operations. The reporting does not characterize whether the promotion signals a succession path or reflects Cogliano's value in player evaluation and development.
